# Engineering practices

General software-engineering practices, independent of any one project. (These are portable, shared rules; project-specific rules — architecture, test mechanics — live in the consuming repo's own docs. The portable git/GitHub-operational practices — branch/commit history, merging, automated-job branches — live in [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md); the mechanics of searching and rewriting text across files — grep/sed sweeps, renames, broken references — live in [the repo-text-sweeps skill](../repo-text-sweeps/SKILL.md); and the practices for writing trustworthy tests — see-it-fail, snapshot/golden discipline, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, coverage gating — live in [the writing-tests skill](../writing-tests/SKILL.md); and how to investigate a bug and pin down its root cause — version-gap triage, re-deriving after a failed fix, probing for a real datapoint — lives in [the bug-investigation skill](../bug-investigation/SKILL.md).)

- Name by scope/responsibility, not technology or mechanism.
- Keep a single source of truth for derived or duplicated data — generate the rest from it instead of hand-editing, and have a test fail if it drifts. Split a fact across more than one place only when a technological constraint forbids a single home, and then have the drift-guard test state, in its own text, the two-or-more places it watches and why the split is forced — so an invisible coupling becomes a self-documenting, reviewed one, and the next reader knows the duplication is deliberate and where its other half lives. When the duplicate mirrors executable logic you can't generate from (e.g. a static list shadowing a set of predicate/matcher functions), drift-guard it by *executing the real logic* against the list in both directions — every entry accepted by some predicate, and every predicate satisfied by some entry — rather than parsing the logic out. When a value must be copied into files that can't share an import (a label spanning a YAML workflow guard and a JS module; a repo slug in prod code and its test), declare it as a `sharedConstants` entry in `.claudinite-checks.json` — its `value`, the expected per-file `counts`, and a `what` naming the places and why — and the basics pack's `shared-constants` check enforces the counts, failing when a rename leaves some copies behind. It counts the *flat* literal (comments included), so keep a guarded value on one line wherever it appears — an occurrence wrapped across a line break is invisible to the check and to a `grep`/`sed` rename alike. For a value that must stay in sync but *changes over time* (a version string bumped each release), set `regex: true` and give a pattern instead of a literal — the check then requires every match to be identical across the declared files, so the guard never needs re-pinning on a bump.
- Honor separation of concerns in what you write — code comments and Markdown instructions alike: when file A uses or references file B (a module A imports, or a doc/procedure set A points to), A may state *what* it needs from B or *that* it delegates to B, but never restate *how* B does its job or re-spell the procedures B owns. B's mechanism lives in one place — with B. Copying it into A leaks B's internals across the boundary and springs the same drift trap as any duplicated source of truth: change B and A's paraphrase silently goes stale, with nothing to catch it. Point to B instead of paraphrasing it.
- Name any file a test autogenerates with `GENERATED` in its filename (e.g. `foo.GENERATED.md`, `foo.baseline.GENERATED.json`) so it's unmistakable at a glance. Don't hand-edit a GENERATED file, and never resolve its merge conflict by hand: take either side to clear the markers, re-run the generator against the merged inputs, and commit its output. Hand-editing desyncs it from its source — and when the other branch changed the generator's logic, only a re-run produces correct values. Automate the "take either side" step itself where you can: assign the file a `merge=ours` `.gitattributes` entry (plus a one-time `git config merge.ours.driver true` per clone) so a conflicting merge on it resolves automatically instead of needing the markers cleared by hand first; `git config rerere.enabled true` similarly replays a manual conflict resolution automatically the next time the same conflict recurs.
- Verify how a platform or runtime actually behaves against authoritative docs or a real run — not against a comment or a prior commit's claim.
- Prove a *behaviour-preserving* optimisation actually preserves behaviour before trusting it — "it should be equivalent" is not evidence. Fingerprint the full outputs (hash them) and exercise the old and new paths across *every* branch (fuzz the inputs that select each), accepting the change only on a bit-identical match. And it is legitimate to leave a hot path un-optimised when the correctness risk of rewriting it outweighs the speed-up — record that as a deliberate call, not an oversight.
- Earn each dependency: prefer a built-in (or a few lines) for a narrow job, and drop one when the assumption that justified it lapses.
- Before adding production code for a raised edge case (a review's "what about scenario X?"), check whether the system's existing composed rules already produce the right answer — behaviour that emerges from a composition of independent rules (a pure reducer, a set of matchers) is often already covered, sometimes on more than one independent count. When it is, add no production code: pin it with a regression test — and an accept criterion under the relevant requirement, where you track those — asserting the contrast case too, so the test would bite if the rule interaction ever changed.
- A bespoke how-to earns its place only by what it adds over authoritative external docs — our own failure modes, gotchas, and the exact path we ran. Before writing one, check it against those docs and keep only the additive parts; a guide that re-explains upstream (often less well) is worse than a link to upstream plus a short gotchas list. And document/recommend only a path you've actually run, not the "standard" or seemingly-better one you haven't.
- Resilience that swallows errors destroys observability — during development, before a solution is proven right, add debugging information first, and remove it later.
- When automating a task that requires live AI conversation context (e.g., a reflection pass over a session), hook it to an existing human workflow event rather than background infrastructure — shell hooks lack conversation access and fire at per-turn granularity, not session-end. The cheapest trigger is often a change to an existing command's definition.
- In a pipeline or CI workflow, treat expected, handled outcomes (known-bad inputs, anticipated stops) as clean exits with a comment — not failures. Reserve the failure signal for genuine breakage; a red run should always be a surprise.
- A live fetch that works on your machine can fail from CI or a sandbox (403/400, a CAPTCHA wall) because the *datacenter IP* is blocked, not the User-Agent — browser-like headers won't change that. Route the fetch through a residential-proxy service (these usually render JS too, so a single-page app records real content) rather than tweaking headers; treat targets that stay blocked even through a proxy as un-cacheable.
- `pkill -f "<pattern>"` matches the *invoking shell's own* command line too, so a pattern naming the process you want also names the shell that typed it — the shell dies, and everything chained after the `pkill` (`;`, `&&`) is silently dropped, with the run reporting only a bare non-zero exit. Never chain a `-f` pkill; and break the self-match by bracketing one character of the pattern (`pkill -f "[h]ttp.server 8099"`), which still matches the target but no longer matches the literal you just typed.
- A cloud/root setup script may start in the repo's *parent* directory, not the checkout — a bare `npm ci` / build there finds no manifest and silently does nothing, surfacing much later as a confusing missing-deps error. Make the setup script `cd` into the checkout before running anything.
- A `Cannot find module …` (or other missing-dependency) error on a *fresh* checkout almost always means the install hasn't run there yet, not a code bug — `node_modules` and other vendored dependency dirs start empty on a clone and on an ephemeral CI/sandbox checkout. Run the install and re-run before hunting for a code-level cause.
- Collapse a property tracked in more than one place (a spec tag, a side manifest, a per-item field) into a single source of truth, preferring a *structural* classifier — one derived from where the item lives (its folder or path) — over a hand-set field: a structural classifier has no field to forget to update and can't desync from the item it classifies.
- Avoid a default value; require it explicitly, or make it structural (derived from where the thing lives). A default moves the real value into a fallback (`x || DEFAULT`) plus a comment documenting it — two things that drift, neither visible at the call site — all to save a little typing. When automation maintains many instances of a config (a fleet of repos, generated project files), have the automation **materialize the explicit value into every file it maintains** instead of interpreting absence: the knob then sits visibly in the exact file where anyone would go to change it, and a missing key becomes drift the automation repairs rather than a case code must interpret (e.g. the fleet baselining writing `"maintenance": { "delivery": "auto" }` into each member's `.claudinite-checks.json`).
- When a check that walks a file tree (an orphan/reachability scan, a doc audit, a lint) must ignore files you don't own — a synced submodule, a vendored dependency, generated output — derive its file set from `git ls-files` rather than a filesystem walk with a hardcoded path-to-skip. There's no exclude path to maintain, it can't desync when an artifact moves, and it stays correct when a new gitignored directory appears. Git already knows what you own; tracked vs. ignored is the exact distinction.
- A check that scans source for a forbidden token (a banned API, an impure import, a DOM specific) must match *code, not prose* — strip comments before you match, or a comment that merely names the token (`// saved in chrome.storage`) fails the build over an English sentence, and the next author who documents the very rule you're enforcing trips it. Strip *string-aware*: a `//` inside `"https://…"` is not a comment, and blindly deleting to end-of-line corrupts real code (and can hide a genuine violation later on that line). The corpus's reusable helper is `stripComments` in [`engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs`](../../../../engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs); a project whose scan can't import it (e.g. a test that runs where the mount is absent) should inline the same string-aware pass and point a comment back at that canonical source.
- A comment should carry the *why* or a cross-file relationship the code can't state itself — not a fact already reconstructable from same-file code plus a known convention (a restated fact drifts out of sync as the code changes, silently). When a comment must name another file, state its exact path in exactly one canonical place and have every other mention point at that reference or the concept, not re-spell the path — a path repeated across many comments turns every future move into comment-churn the code itself never needed.

# Testing practices

Portable practices for writing tests you can actually trust — proving a test fails before relying on it, snapshot/golden discipline, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, and how to gate a fuzzy quality metric. These are project-agnostic; a consuming repo's own test *mechanics* (runner, layout, which suites exist) stay in its own docs. (General software-engineering practices live in [the engineering-practices skill](../engineering-practices/SKILL.md); CI-trigger rules and the `GITHUB_TOKEN` workflow-recursion gotcha live in [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md).)

- See a test fail before you trust it: write it red before the fix (green after), or break what it guards and watch it go red. A test that has never failed proves nothing. For a **refusal/negative** test — one asserting a guard yields *nothing* — the write-it-red-first branch is unavailable: the pre-change code also yielded nothing, so the test passes from birth and proves nothing. See-it-fail there **must** be the second method — mutate the new guard (weaken it), watch the test bite, then restore it.
- Before trusting a new transform/normalizer, run it over the *real existing corpus* it will process, not just hand-picked test inputs — the live data exposes edge cases your examples won't. (A hostname-apex helper passed its tests but mis-stripped `tel-aviv.gov.il` → `gov.il`; the gap only surfaced when the function was run over the actual list of existing URLs.) Relatedly, prefer a generic structural rule over a hand-maintained list of special cases: the enumerated list needs per-instance upkeep and silently has gaps, while a rule keyed on structure (e.g. "a known registry label under any 2-letter ccTLD") covers the whole class at once.
- A test that stubs the exact boundary where the bug lives can't catch that bug — it guards only the shape it asserts, not the runtime effect. Say what it can't catch.
- Prefer a single shared double; but when a subsystem is faked by more than one (a minimal unit stub vs. a faithful harness that boots the real module), a new call into the faked surface must be taught to **every** double, or the untaught one breaks — and the faithful harness turns an unmodeled API into a confusing **far-away** failure (a DOM-snapshot pixel-diff, not a local error at the call site). After adding a call into a faked boundary, find every double of it and extend each.
- A traceability/coverage gate that requires every spec item be *claimed* by some test of one fixed kind proves only that it's claimed, not that it's verified. When items differ in kind, the gate green-lights claims that kind can't check — a pixel snapshot "covers" a click's tab-opening it can never observe, or a state the case never renders (and can't, when the data can't reach it). Segment the gate by the verification each item needs (route behavior to a behavior test, rendering to a snapshot) rather than forcing every item onto one mechanism. (A UI-snapshot coverage gate parked behavioral leaves `9.1`–`9.3`/`3.4` and an unreachable `8.6` on cases that render none of them — issue #429.)
- A golden/snapshot test whose expected artifact is hand-authored to mirror what production renders is a parallel implementation: it drifts from the real output and can't catch changes to the renderer (a hand-built UI gallery even faked a state the app never shows). Drive the snapshot through the real code path, faking only its inputs.
- A snapshot/golden test that depends on the current date/time must inject a fixed reference instant, not read the real clock — else a fixed-date fixture silently rots as wall-clock time passes ("this year" becomes "past" next year). Thread the reference time through the code under test, defaulting to the real clock in production. When retrofitting such a rule into an existing fixture suite, pin the reference instant so existing fixtures land on the same side they were authored for — so only the cases that deliberately exercise the new rule change and the diff stays small and reviewable, rather than a sprawling baseline churn that buries the intended change.
- A new **e2e / heavy-browser** test must go green at least twice in CI before merging — one green run doesn't rule out a flake. This applies only to that class (the real-Chrome `test/fullBrowserHeavyTests/` suites); the deterministic offline/unit/integration tests don't touch a live browser or network, so one green run is enough for them.
- A test that can only run remotely (e.g. CI-only) must diagnose itself: on failure, dump the observed state, not just an assertion. It must also be *hang-proof* — bound every `await` (a timeout race) and set a test-level timeout — so a failure fails fast with that diagnostic instead of burning the whole job's timeout. An unbounded await on something that never settles (e.g. a callback that silently never fires) turns a 5-second failure into a 20-minute hang, and each CI-only iteration already costs a full round-trip.
- To test code that drives a real browser or other external runtime in CI, prefer a *self-authored hermetic input* (e.g. a `data:` URL whose own script reproduces the behavior) over hitting a live third-party target — the live target is non-deterministic and often bot-blocked from a CI/datacenter IP, so it flakes or can't run, while a self-authored input exercises the same engine deterministically. (The SPA-render fallback's CI test renders a `data:` URL whose script fills an empty root, not a real SPA — #310.)
- Gate a fuzzy quality metric (a coverage %, not a binary pass) behind a high-watermark: refresh the artifact and ratchet the watermark up locally, keep CI read-only (assert against the committed baseline, never rewrite it), and re-baseline by hand only when a deliberate change legitimately moves it — a number that can only climb catches a silent regression without flapping on noise. When the population it covers can *grow* (e.g. new test cases), store the set the watermark was computed over and gate only over the cases shared with it, so a newly added item is excluded rather than dragging the aggregate below the bar; re-anchor the watermark when the set changes. (A single aggregate watermark can then be re-anchored over a regression bundled into the *same* change as a set change — store per-item bars if that must be caught.)
- For behavior a person must sign off on (a third-party integration, an extraction result), keep a layer of declarative, human-reviewed expectation files — distinct from the unit tests, which nobody reads for *intent* — and cover every behavior change with a minimal, representative case there (one behavior per case, no incidental complexity), since that case is what gets reviewed.
- When a snapshot/golden test fails because the output *legitimately* moved (the pixels or bytes changed for a real reason), don't quietly regenerate the baseline to go green — an unreviewed baseline change is an unreviewed behavior change. Surface the diff (committed **expected**, newly-rendered **actual**, highlighted **diff**) and get owner approval before re-baselining; until then keep the *reverted* baseline committed so the branch honestly shows the test red-pending — never commit the new baseline first.
- When a test asserts exact values extracted from a captured artifact (a cached page, a recorded response), record and commit the artifact *first*, then read the expected values off the committed file — don't hand-write the expectations from memory or a live view and hope they match. Guessing the value desyncs the test from the real fixture; reading it off the committed bytes can't.
- A test that maintains a committed artifact should regenerate it into the working tree deterministically (no timestamps, so an unchanged run yields no diff) and skip the write under CI — never shell out to git from a test. Commit the artifact through the normal review flow, like a snapshot.
- Render a UI *image* golden with the engine that matches the surface, and prefer the deterministic one. A surface that is inline-styled SVG, or flexbox-only markup authored for it, renders **bit-exact** through a headless rasterizer (e.g. satori → SVG, resvg → PNG) driven by the shipped code, using **bundled** fonts, never system fonts, and a pinned locale — demand a **zero-pixel** diff there. But that rasterizer has no CSS engine and draws no native widgets: a full shipped page using CSS **grid**, custom properties (`var()`), `@media`, **emoji**, or **form controls** (a range slider, radio, `<select>`) is beyond it — screenshot that with a **headless browser** instead, and allow a *small* diff tolerance (browser antialiasing varies across machines, so it isn't bit-exact). Match the engine to the surface; never reshape the product to fit the rasterizer. (A rasterized popup golden works only because the popup was authored flexbox-only — the moment a surface needs grid/vars/widgets, it needs a browser.) Since the browser goldens aren't gate-able bit-exact and a runner may lack the browser, let those cases **self-skip** where it's absent so the deterministic cases still gate.
- To image-golden a surface your code **injects into a host page** (a control mounted into a third-party toolbar), render it against a **committed capture of the real host DOM with its computed styles flattened inline** — the deterministic rasterizer reads only inline styles, and the host's own stylesheet is not yours to ship. Mount it with the **shipped injector** (so the golden proves the placement, not a hand-placed copy), and name the model's boundary honestly: substituted icon-font glyphs, an approximated host chrome (a captured sample is spec, not folklore — the origin lesson of a supported-targets matrix).

Based on the search results, here's what I found about OpenTable's affiliate program and how to join:

## OpenTable Affiliate Program Overview

The OpenTable affiliate program allows travel, food, and lifestyle influencers to monetize their dining recommendations by connecting their audience to the world's leading restaurant reservation platform, with partners earning commissions on seated diners.

## How to Join

To apply, you need to go to OpenTable's developer portal and start the application process by clicking on "Become a Partner." The OpenTable affiliate program is not open to everyone, and approval is on a case-by-case basis.

The entire process, from registration to the creation of the unique reservation links, may take at least two to three weeks.

## Commission Structure

All new affiliates start as non-revenue partners, but once they have consistently referred over 100 reservation seats per month, they are eligible for sharing the revenue and gaining commissions.

## Important Note About Impact Network

While OpenTable has historically appeared on networks like CJ or Impact for specific campaigns (or via their parent company Booking Holdings), the core reservation partnership is managed directly through the OpenTable Partner Program (developer/business portal).

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Trainline Partnerize affiliate deep link format:

## Trainline Affiliate Program

Trainline's affiliate partner links and reporting is managed through the Partnerize platform.

## Partnerize Deep Link Format

The general Partnerize affiliate link format using `prf.hn` and `camref` is:

The default format is `https://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX`

You can customize these links with additional parameters:

- **PUBREF** (publisher reference): `http://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/pubref:newcastle`
- **ADREF** (ad reference): `http://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/ar:london`
- **Destination/Deeplink**: `http://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/destination:http://www.advertiser.com`

You can also combine all three parameters: `https://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/pubref:newcastle/ar:london/destination:http://www.advertiser.com`

For Trainline specifically, you would need to replace the `XXXX` in `camref:XXXX` with your unique campaign reference identifier provided by Trainline through the Partnerize dashboard.

/* ---------- Monetization: affiliate / referral IDs ----------
 *
 * These are NOT secrets — they ship in the client, like the analytics token in
 * js/analytics.js — and they are empty by default: every link below works as a
 * plain deep link, and starts tagging referrals the moment an ID is filled in.
 *
 * TO MONETIZE, join the partner programmes and paste the IDs here:
 *   - Awin (awin.com) — one publisher account covers Trainline (and many other
 *     UK travel/dining merchants). awinAffiliateId is your publisher ID;
 *     trainlineAwinMid is Trainline's advertiser ID from your Awin dashboard.
 *   - OpenTable (opentable.com/affiliate-program) — opentableRef is the `ref`
 *     value OpenTable assigns you.
 *   - Booking.com (partners.booking.com) — bookingAid is your `aid` number.
 *   - GetYourGuide (partner.getyourguide.com) — gygPartnerId.
 * A link whose programme IDs are unset simply stays untagged — partial set-up
 * is fine.
 */
export const AFFILIATES = {
  awinAffiliateId: "",
  trainlineAwinMid: "",
  opentableRef: "",
  bookingAid: "",
  gygPartnerId: "",
};

input.title: Monetization: join the 4 affiliate programmes and paste the IDs into js/places.js
input.body:
The booking buttons on committed places (PR #157, #158) work today as plain deep links and start earning referral commission the moment the affiliate IDs are filled in. All the code is done — `js/places.js` builds every link and tags it automatically once its ID is set. **The only remaining work is joining the programmes**, which each partner runs where *it* chooses (researched 2026-07-29).

Where the IDs go — the `AFFILIATES` block at the top of [`js/places.js`](../blob/main/js/places.js):

```js
export const AFFILIATES = {
  opentableRef: "",      // ← step 4
  trainlineCamref: "",   // ← step 2
  awinAffiliateId: "",   // ← step 1
  bookingAwinMid: "",    // ← step 1
  gygPartnerId: "",      // ← step 3
};
```

Partial set-up is fine: each link stays a working untagged deep link until its own ID arrives. Suggested order = fastest payoff first.

### 1. Booking.com — via Awin (days to approve) → `awinAffiliateId` + `bookingAwinMid`
Booking.com runs its affiliate programme on the Awin network (up to ~4% of the booking).
- [ ] Create an Awin **publisher** account: https://ui.awin.com/publisher-signup/en/awin/step1 — describe EdFringeNow (a free Edinburgh Fringe day-planner that links visitors to hotels near their committed plans). Awin may ask a small refundable deposit to verify you.
- [ ] Once the publisher account is live, find **Booking.com** under Advertisers (regional programmes exist — join the one covering the UK) and apply: https://www.awin.com/us/advertisers/partner/booking.com
- [ ] After acceptance, copy two numbers from the Awin dashboard: your **publisher ID** → `awinAffiliateId`, and Booking.com's **advertiser ID ("MID")** shown on its programme profile → `bookingAwinMid`.
- [ ] Verify: commit a hotel (type "Malmaison") → the button's URL should now start `https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=…` and end with the Booking.com search inside `ued=`.

### 2. Trainline — via Partnerize → `trainlineCamref`
Trainline's programme runs on the Partnerize platform (commission on ticket sales, 30-day cookie).
- [ ] Apply at https://www.thetrainline.com/about-us/partnerships/affiliates — applications are reviewed, then you get a welcome pack and Partnerize dashboard access.
- [ ] In Partnerize, copy your **campaign reference** — the `camref:XXXX` token in your tracking link → paste just the `XXXX` part into `trainlineCamref`.
- [ ] Verify: commit "Edinburgh Waverley" → the button's URL should become `https://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/destination:…/stations/edinburgh`.

### 3. GetYourGuide (days to approve, ~8% of the activity price) → `gygPartnerId`
- [ ] Sign up at https://partner.getyourguide.com — basic details about the site and audience; approval typically takes a few days.
- [ ] Copy the **partner ID** from the partner dashboard → `gygPartnerId`. (Payout threshold €50; commission pays out after the activity happens.)
- [ ] Verify: commit "Camera Obscura" → the button's URL should carry `&partner_id=…`.

### 4. OpenTable (slowest — treat as optional) → `opentableRef`
Approval is case-by-case via the "Become a Partner" application on OpenTable's partner/developer portal, takes ~2–3 weeks, and **new affiliates start non-revenue**: revenue share opens up only after consistently referring ~100+ seated diners a month. Worth doing eventually — restaurant/café/pub is the most-typed place kind — but don't block on it.
- [ ] Apply via OpenTable's partner portal ("Become a Partner").
- [ ] Paste the assigned `ref` value → `opentableRef`.
- [ ] Verify: commit a restaurant → the button's URL should carry `&ref=…`.

### Done when
- [ ] At least Booking.com + GetYourGuide IDs are live in `js/places.js` (a one-line change each; the unit tests in `js/__tests__/places.test.mjs` assert the tagging shape, and the footer already carries the commission disclosure).

Sources: [Trainline affiliate programme](https://www.thetrainline.com/about-us/partnerships/affiliates) · [Awin publisher sign-up](https://ui.awin.com/publisher-signup/en/awin/step1) · [Booking.com on Awin](https://www.awin.com/us/advertisers/partner/booking.com) · [GetYourGuide partner programme](https://partner.getyourguide.com) · [Partnerize link format](https://docs.fmtc.co/kb/partnerize)

{"number":157,"title":"Non-show places: geocode "Type a place" into real destinations, with partner booking links","body":"## What

The "Not a show? Type a place" box previously stored a bare text label — no pin, no route, no plan. Now **Find on map** (or Enter) geocodes the query with Nominatim (OpenStreetMap's geocoder — no API key, same stack as the Leaflet/OSM map):

- **One match** commits directly; **several** render candidate rows (kind icon + name + street) to pick from; **none / offline** falls back to keeping the text as a note — which now renders its own coordinate-less plan node ("🚶 make your own way → 📝 My cousin's flat") instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin with tooltip, route leg with the ✓-arrival check, plan destination node with slack chip, Google Maps directions link, and the show list constrained to what you can slip in before it. Typing "Edinburgh Waverley" + your train time now literally answers *"which shows can I catch before my train?"*.

## Monetization

Bookable places carry a partner pill on the plan node, styled like the shows' "Buy ahead" pill:

| Place kind | Partner | Link |
|---|---|---|
| restaurant / café / pub | OpenTable | search pinned to the place's name + coords |
| train station | Trainline | via Awin deep-link wrapper |
| hotel | Booking.com | search for the property in Edinburgh |
| attraction / museum / historic | GetYourGuide | tours & tickets search |

Links work as plain deep links today and start tagging referrals the moment the affiliate IDs in `js/places.js` are filled in (its **TO MONETIZE** block documents each programme to join, mirroring `js/analytics.js`'s TO ENABLE pattern). The pills use `rel="sponsored"`, and the footer discloses the commission.

## Live-API findings (probed, not guessed)

The sandbox can't reach nominatim.openstreetmap.org, so the query shape was probed from a throwaway GitHub Actions workflow (deleted before this PR), and the captured responses are committed verbatim as test fixtures:

- `bounded=1` restricts search to amenity tags inside the box — it returns the pub/café *inside* Waverley's concourse but **not Edinburgh Waverley station itself**, and finds no "The Piemaker" at all. The shipped call is therefore **unbounded with a viewbox bias**, plus a client-side Edinburgh box filter (which also drops "Camera Obscura" hits from Germany, London and Moscow).
- One landmark geocodes as several same-named hits a block apart (Waverley = station node + building outline + roof + two platform stops): same-label nearby hits dedupe, with typed hits (station, arts centre) upgrading untyped ones (streets, roofs) — so "Summerhall" resolves to the venue, not its street.

## Tests & verification

- `js/__tests__/places.test.mjs` (13 cases) pins the URL builder, parser, kind buckets and partner links against the committed real fixtures; every guard was mutation-checked red before trusting it. New `js/__tests__` glob wired into `package.json` and `scripts/verify.sh`.
- Full flow driven in headless Chromium against the served site with Nominatim route-stubbed by the same fixtures: candidate picking, single-match auto-commit, partner pill hrefs, place pin, constrained list heading, Maps link coords, note fallback, and commitment removal — 14/14 checks pass. `npm run verify` green.

Screenshot of the result (train commitment):

- plan: *You are here → 3 min walk → 🚆 16:25 Edinburgh Waverley, 38 min to spare* with a **Train times & tickets · Trainline** pill, station pinned on the map with the ✓ 16:25 arrival check.

input.body:
## What

The "Not a show? Type a place" box previously stored a bare text label — no pin, no route, no plan. Now **Find on map** (or Enter) geocodes the query with Nominatim (OpenStreetMap's geocoder — no API key, same stack as the Leaflet/OSM map):

- **One match** commits directly; **several** render candidate rows (kind icon + name + street) to pick from; **none / offline** falls back to keeping the text as a note — which now renders its own coordinate-less plan node ("🚶 make your own way → 📝 My cousin's flat") instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin with tooltip, route leg with the ✓-arrival check, plan destination node with slack chip, Google Maps directions link, and the show list constrained to what you can slip in before it. Typing "Edinburgh Waverley" + your train time now literally answers *"which shows can I catch before my train?"*.
- The remembered Now page (#155) snapshots place/note commitments too, so a committed place survives a reload with its pin and plan intact.

## Monetization

A committed bookable place asks **"Need to book it?"** outright on its plan card — a bold bordered box with a big partner button and a corner ×. Dismissing shrinks it to a quiet pill (the link survives, the question doesn't); a fresh commitment re-asks. Links pre-fill what the user already told us:

| Place kind | Partner | Programme | Deep link carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| restaurant / café / pub | OpenTable | OpenTable partner programme (`ref`) | venue name + coords, `covers=2`, the **committed time** as `dateTime` |
| train station | Trainline | **Partnerize** (`camref` click-wrap) | the station's own page (Waverley → `/stations/edinburgh`; unverified slugs fall back to the homepage) |
| hotel | Booking.com | **Awin** (`awinmid` wrap) | property search + **checkin/checkout tonight** (month-boundary-safe) |
| attraction / museum / historic | GetYourGuide | GetYourGuide partner programme (`partner_id`) | tours & tickets search |

Links work as plain deep links today and start tagging referrals the moment the affiliate IDs in `js/places.js` are filled in — **#161 tracks the sign-up path for each programme step-by-step** (researched: Trainline runs on Partnerize, not Awin; Booking.com runs on Awin, not a bare `aid`). The buttons use `rel="sponsored"`, and the footer discloses the commission.

## Live-API findings (probed, not guessed)

The sandbox can't reach nominatim.openstreetmap.org, so the query shape was probed from a throwaway GitHub Actions workflow (deleted before this PR), and the captured responses are committed verbatim as test fixtures:

- `bounded=1` restricts search to amenity tags inside the box — it returns the pub/café *inside* Waverley's concourse but **not Edinburgh Waverley station itself**, and finds no "The Piemaker" at all. The shipped call is therefore **unbounded with a viewbox bias**, plus a client-side Edinburgh box filter (which also drops "Camera Obscura" hits from Germany, London and Moscow).
- One landmark geocodes as several same-named hits a block apart (Waverley = station node + building outline + roof + two platform stops): same-label nearby hits dedupe, with typed hits (station, arts centre) upgrading untyped ones (streets, roofs) — so "Summerhall" resolves to the venue, not its street.

## Merge-with-main integration

Merging main's remembered Now page + filters (#155) surfaced two real integration bugs, both fixed in the merge commit:

- The plan snapshot didn't know `destPlace`/`destNote`, so a saved place commitment restored as dead text.
- Closing the constraint panel clamps the hidden time-wheels' `scrollTop` and fires a final scroll event; the settle handler read that as the user picking a new time and **wiped the just-made commitment**. It now ignores hidden wheels.

## Tests & verification

- `js/__tests__/places.test.mjs` (15 cases) pins the URL builder, parser, kind buckets and partner links against the committed real fixtures; every guard was mutation-checked or written red-first. New `js/__tests__` glob wired into `package.json` and `scripts/verify.sh`.
- Full flow driven in headless Chromium against the served site with Nominatim route-stubbed by the same fixtures: candidate picking, single-match auto-commit, the booking ask → dismiss → re-ask cycle, deep-link params, reload persistence, place pin, constrained list heading, Maps link coords, note fallback, and commitment removal — **16/16 checks pass**. `npm run verify` green.

places: geocode 'Type a place' into real destinations, with partner booking links

The 'Not a show? Type a place' box previously stored a bare text label —
no pin, no route, no plan. Now 'Find on map' geocodes the query with
Nominatim (OpenStreetMap — no API key, matching the Leaflet/OSM stack):

- One match commits directly; several render candidate rows to pick from;
  none (or offline) falls back to keeping the text as a note, which now
  renders its own coordinate-less plan node instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin,
  route leg with the arrival check, plan destination node, Google Maps
  link, and the show list constrained to what fits before it.
- Bookable places carry a partner pill on the plan (monetization):
  restaurants/cafés/pubs -> OpenTable, stations -> Trainline (Awin),
  hotels -> Booking.com, attractions -> GetYourGuide. Links work plainly
  today and start tagging referrals once the affiliate IDs in js/places.js
  are filled in (see its TO MONETIZE block); the footer discloses the
  commission.

The geocoder call was probed against the live API from an Actions runner
(the sandbox can't reach it): bounded=1 searches only amenity tags inside
the box — it misses Edinburgh Waverley entirely — so the search is
unbounded with a viewbox bias plus a client-side Edinburgh filter, and
same-named hits a block apart (station node vs building vs platforms)
dedupe with typed hits upgrading untyped ones. The captured responses are
committed as fixtures under js/__tests__/fixtures/nominatim/ and pin the
parser in js/__tests__/places.test.mjs (new js/ test glob wired into
package.json + scripts/verify.sh).

Closes #158

places: geocode 'Type a place' into real destinations, with partner booking links

The 'Not a show? Type a place' box previously stored a bare text label —
no pin, no route, no plan. Now 'Find on map' geocodes the query with
Nominatim (OpenStreetMap — no API key, matching the Leaflet/OSM stack):

- One match commits directly; several render candidate rows to pick from;
  none (or offline) falls back to keeping the text as a note, which now
  renders its own coordinate-less plan node instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin,
  route leg with the arrival check, plan destination node, Google Maps
  link, and the show list constrained to what fits before it.
- Bookable places carry a partner pill on the plan (monetization):
  restaurants/cafés/pubs -> OpenTable, stations -> Trainline (Awin),
  hotels -> Booking.com, attractions -> GetYourGuide. Links work plainly
  today and start tagging referrals once the affiliate IDs in js/places.js
  are filled in (see its TO MONETIZE block); the footer discloses the
  commission.

The geocoder call was probed against the live API from an Actions runner
(the sandbox can't reach it): bounded=1 searches only amenity tags inside
the box — it misses Edinburgh Waverley entirely — so the search is
unbounded with a viewbox bias plus a client-side Edinburgh filter, and
same-named hits a block apart (station node vs building vs platforms)
dedupe with typed hits upgrading untyped ones. The captured responses are
committed as fixtures under js/__tests__/fixtures/nominatim/ and pin the
parser in js/__tests__/places.test.mjs (new js/ test glob wired into
package.json + scripts/verify.sh).

places: geocode 'Type a place' into real destinations, with partner booking links

The 'Not a show? Type a place' box previously stored a bare text label —
no pin, no route, no plan. Now 'Find on map' geocodes the query with
Nominatim (OpenStreetMap — no API key, matching the Leaflet/OSM stack):

- One match commits directly; several render candidate rows to pick from;
  none (or offline) falls back to keeping the text as a note, which now
  renders its own coordinate-less plan node instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin,
  route leg with the arrival check, plan destination node, Google Maps
  link, and the show list constrained to what fits before it.
- Bookable places carry a partner pill on the plan (monetization):
  restaurants/cafés/pubs -> OpenTable, stations -> Trainline (Awin),
  hotels -> Booking.com, attractions -> GetYourGuide. Links work plainly
  today and start tagging referrals once the affiliate IDs in js/places.js
  are filled in (see its TO MONETIZE block); the footer discloses the
  commission.

The geocoder call was probed against the live API from an Actions runner
(the sandbox can't reach it): bounded=1 searches only amenity tags inside
the box — it misses Edinburgh Waverley entirely — so the search is
unbounded with a viewbox bias plus a client-side Edinburgh filter, and
same-named hits a block apart (station node vs building vs platforms)
dedupe with typed hits upgrading untyped ones. The captured responses are
committed as fixtures under js/__tests__/fixtures/nominatim/ and pin the
parser in js/__tests__/places.test.mjs (new js/ test glob wired into
package.json + scripts/verify.sh).

Closes #158

places: geocode 'Type a place' into real destinations, with partner booking links

The 'Not a show? Type a place' box previously stored a bare text label —
no pin, no route, no plan. Now 'Find on map' geocodes the query with
Nominatim (OpenStreetMap — no API key, matching the Leaflet/OSM stack):

- One match commits directly; several render candidate rows to pick from;
  none (or offline) falls back to keeping the text as a note, which now
  renders its own coordinate-less plan node instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin,
  route leg with the arrival check, plan destination node, Google Maps
  link, and the show list constrained to what fits before it.
- Bookable places carry a partner pill on the plan (monetization):
  restaurants/cafés/pubs -> OpenTable, stations -> Trainline (Awin),
  hotels -> Booking.com, attractions -> GetYourGuide. Links work plainly
  today and start tagging referrals once the affiliate IDs in js/places.js
  are filled in (see its TO MONETIZE block); the footer discloses the
  commission.

The geocoder call was probed against the live API from an Actions runner
(the sandbox can't reach it): bounded=1 searches only amenity tags inside
the box — it misses Edinburgh Waverley entirely — so the search is
unbounded with a viewbox bias plus a client-side Edinburgh filter, and
same-named hits a block apart (station node vs building vs platforms)
dedupe with typed hits upgrading untyped ones. The captured responses are
committed as fixtures under js/__tests__/fixtures/nominatim/ and pin the
parser in js/__tests__/places.test.mjs (new js/ test glob wired into
package.json + scripts/verify.sh).

Closes #158

The 'Not a show? Type a place' box previously stored a bare text label —
no pin, no route, no plan. Now 'Find on map' geocodes the query with
Nominatim (OpenStreetMap — no API key, matching the Leaflet/OSM stack):

- One match commits directly; several render candidate rows to pick from;
  none (or offline) falls back to keeping the text as a note, which now
  renders its own coordinate-less plan node instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin,
  route leg with the arrival check, plan destination node, Google Maps
  link, and the show list constrained to what fits before it.
- Bookable places carry a partner pill on the plan (monetization):
  restaurants/cafés/pubs -> OpenTable, stations -> Trainline (Awin),
  hotels -> Booking.com, attractions -> GetYourGuide. Links work plainly
  today and start tagging referrals once the affiliate IDs in js/places.js
  are filled in (see its TO MONETIZE block); the footer discloses the
  commission.

The geocoder call was probed against the live API from an Actions runner
(the sandbox can't reach it): bounded=1 searches only amenity tags inside
the box — it misses Edinburgh Waverley entirely — so the search is
unbounded with a viewbox bias plus a client-side Edinburgh filter, and
same-named hits a block apart (station node vs building vs platforms)
dedupe with typed hits upgrading untyped ones. The captured responses are
committed as fixtures under js/__tests__/fixtures/nominatim/ and pin the
parser in js/__tests__/places.test.mjs (new js/ test glob wired into
package.json + scripts/verify.sh).

content.text:
Everything is shipped and the reply is below. CI on the merged head hadn't been scheduled yet at my last check — the same verify suite is green locally and was green on both prior heads; my PR subscription will wake this session if it fails.

**Comment class: feature** (booking CTA; selection-aware deep links) **+ other** (the cousin's-flat question, answered below; the research/tracking-issue task).

**The bold call to action is live.** After committing a bookable destination, the plan card now asks **"Need to book it?"** in a bordered box with a big full-width partner button ("🍺 Book a table · OpenTable") and a little × in the corner — screenshots above. The × doesn't throw the link away: it shrinks the question down to the previous quiet pill, and committing a new place re-asks. Verified end-to-end in Chromium (16/16 checks), including the ask → dismiss → re-ask cycle.

**"My cousin's flat" — what that is.** That's the *fallback* for exactly the places that **aren't** commercial: when you type something the geocoder can't find (a friend's flat, "the meeting point", anywhere with no map presence), the app keeps your text as a note commitment instead of silently losing it. It renders a 📝 plan node with "make your own way" as the connector — because with no coordinates we can't route or book anything. So no commercial entity is involved there by design; the booking question only appears on places we actually resolved to something bookable.

**The links now carry the user's selections.** They already targeted the right partner per kind; now they're deep links built from what the user told us: OpenTable gets the venue's name + coordinates *and the committed time* (`covers=2&dateTime=…`), Booking.com gets the property *and tonight's checkin/checkout* (month-boundary-safe), and Trainline deep-links the committed station's own page — with a catch my research caught: Waverley's Trainline slug is `/stations/edinburgh`, not a guessable `edinburgh-waverley`, so the slug map holds only verified entries and unknown stations fall back to the homepage rather than a 404. All unit-tested red-first (15 cases).

**Tracking issue filed: [#161](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/161).** The research corrected two assumptions from my first cut — Trainline's programme runs on **Partnerize** (camref links), not Awin, and Booking.com's runs on **Awin**, not a bare `aid` param — so I rewired `js/places.js` to tag through each programme's real mechanism. The issue is a per-partner checklist in payoff order: exact sign-up URL, what to say, where the ID appears in each dashboard, which field it goes into, and how to verify each link switches on. OpenTable is flagged honestly as slowest (case-by-case approval, non-revenue until ~100 seated diners/month).

One more thing you should know: while pushing, main moved and PR #157 hit a merge conflict. Merging main surfaced two real integration bugs between our branches, both fixed and pinned by new browser checks: the new "remembered Now page" (#155) didn't snapshot place/note commitments (they'd restore as dead text), and closing the commitment panel fired a stray scroll event that could *wipe a just-made commitment* via the time wheels. `npm run verify` and the full Chromium flow are green on the merged result.

> ✅ **All done — PR #157 updated (booking CTA + selection-aware referral links + main merged), issue #161 tracks the affiliate sign-ups.** Say "LGTM" to merge. Your side: work through #161's checklist and paste the IDs into `js/places.js` — revenue switches on per-partner as each ID lands.

input.body:
## What

The "Not a show? Type a place" box previously stored a bare text label — no pin, no route, no plan. Now **Find on map** (or Enter) geocodes the query with Nominatim (OpenStreetMap's geocoder — no API key, same stack as the Leaflet/OSM map):

- **One match** commits directly; **several** render candidate rows (kind icon + name + street) to pick from; **none / offline** falls back to keeping the text as a note — which now renders its own coordinate-less plan node ("🚶 make your own way → 📝 My cousin's flat") instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin with tooltip, route leg with the ✓-arrival check, plan destination node with slack chip, Google Maps directions link, and the show list constrained to what you can slip in before it. Typing "Edinburgh Waverley" + your train time now literally answers *"which shows can I catch before my train?"*.
- The remembered Now page (#155) snapshots place/note commitments too, so a committed place survives a reload with its pin and plan intact.

## Monetization

A committed bookable place asks **"Need to book it?"** outright on its plan card — a bold bordered box with a big partner button and a corner ×. Dismissing shrinks it to a quiet pill (the link survives, the question doesn't); a fresh commitment re-asks. Links pre-fill what the user already told us:

| Place kind | Partner | Programme | Deep link carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| restaurant / café / pub | OpenTable | OpenTable partner programme (`ref`) | venue name + coords, `covers=2`, the **committed time** as `dateTime` |
| train station | Trainline | **Partnerize** (`camref` click-wrap) | the station's own page (Waverley → `/stations/edinburgh`; unverified slugs fall back to the homepage) |
| hotel | Booking.com | **Awin** (`awinmid` wrap) | property search + **checkin/checkout tonight** (month-boundary-safe) |
| attraction / museum / historic | GetYourGuide | GetYourGuide partner programme (`partner_id`) | tours & tickets search |

Links work as plain deep links today and start tagging referrals the moment the affiliate IDs in `js/places.js` are filled in — **#161 tracks the sign-up path for each programme step-by-step** (researched: Trainline runs on Partnerize, not Awin; Booking.com runs on Awin, not a bare `aid`). The buttons use `rel="sponsored"`, and the footer discloses the commission.

## Live-API findings (probed, not guessed)

The sandbox can't reach nominatim.openstreetmap.org, so the query shape was probed from a throwaway GitHub Actions workflow (deleted before this PR), and the captured responses are committed verbatim as test fixtures:

- `bounded=1` restricts search to amenity tags inside the box — it returns the pub/café *inside* Waverley's concourse but **not Edinburgh Waverley station itself**, and finds no "The Piemaker" at all. The shipped call is therefore **unbounded with a viewbox bias**, plus a client-side Edinburgh box filter (which also drops "Camera Obscura" hits from Germany, London and Moscow).
- One landmark geocodes as several same-named hits a block apart (Waverley = station node + building outline + roof + two platform stops): same-label nearby hits dedupe, with typed hits (station, arts centre) upgrading untyped ones (streets, roofs) — so "Summerhall" resolves to the venue, not its street.

## Integration with main (rebased, linear)

Bringing the branch up to date with main's remembered Now page + filters (#155, #163) surfaced two real integration bugs, fixed in the final commit:

- The plan snapshot didn't know `destPlace`/`destNote`, so a saved place commitment restored as dead text.
- Closing the constraint panel clamps the hidden time-wheels' `scrollTop` and fires a final scroll event; the settle handler read that as the user picking a new time and **wiped the just-made commitment**. It now ignores hidden wheels.

## Tests & verification

- `js/__tests__/places.test.mjs` (15 cases) pins the URL builder, parser, kind buckets and partner links against the committed real fixtures; every guard was mutation-checked or written red-first. New `js/__tests__` glob wired into `package.json` and `scripts/verify.sh`.
- Full flow driven in headless Chromium against the served site with Nominatim route-stubbed by the same fixtures: candidate picking, single-match auto-commit, the booking ask → dismiss → re-ask cycle, deep-link params, reload persistence, place pin, constrained list heading, Maps link coords, note fallback, and commitment removal — **16/16 checks pass** on the rebased branch. `npm run verify` green.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/EdFringeNow/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

The portable recipe for landing the change in front of the owner on `main` — the *mechanics* behind the owner's merge-to-main command (the owner's preferences own the trigger *phrase*; this file owns the *how*). Invoked through the `merge-to-main` skill (this skill); this doc stays the canonical recipe.

**A project's bespoke merge policy overrides this default.** Most projects need nothing here — this default is the whole story. A project that genuinely diverges (a different merge method, a CI/twice-green gate, an extra approval) **states so by naming its merge-policy file explicitly in its own `CLAUDE.md`**. When that declaration is present, read that file first and let it override the divergent points below; when it's absent, follow this default as-is. Don't go hunting for a policy file that the project's `CLAUDE.md` doesn't name.

## Recipe (~4 calls)

1. Load both GitHub tools in **one** `ToolSearch`: `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request`.
2. No PR open for the branch yet? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); end the body with `Closes #<issue>`, and take the PR number from the returned URL.
3. Gate on CI **only if the repo has it** — a workflow that actually runs on PRs/pushes. `workflow_call`-only reusable workflows (this repo hosts some) are *not* CI: they never run here, so a non-empty `.github/workflows/` alone proves nothing; check the PR for check runs instead. No CI → no gate; don't wait for checks that will never come.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Merge directly — don't pre-read status; the call fails loudly if it isn't mergeable.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.

The two divergent points — **`squash`** as the method and **CI gating** — are exactly what a bespoke policy file changes.

## After the merge: capture the conversation (every session, every user)

Once the merge has landed and local `main` is synced, run the growth pack's capture step:
`node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>` (from the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`), `<n>` being the issue your `Closes #<issue>` named. Deterministic, seconds-long; it pushes the conversation to the orphan `conversation-logs` branch. It runs **here, in-session, because it needs the live transcript** — the lessons extraction then happens later in the repo's scheduled `conversation-extract` task (MCP-native, with a rethink window), so there is nothing to schedule and no in-session lessons pass ([the pack README](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) owns the standard). A later merge in the same session just runs capture again — it captures the delta. In the rare repo that removed the `grow_with_claudinite` pack from `.claudinite-checks.json`, skip this step.

## Don't

- **Don't** re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge; trust it.

The 'Not a show? Type a place' box previously stored a bare text label —
no pin, no route, no plan. Now 'Find on map' geocodes the query with
Nominatim (OpenStreetMap — no API key, matching the Leaflet/OSM stack):

- One match commits directly; several render candidate rows to pick from;
  none (or offline) falls back to keeping the text as a note, which now
  renders its own coordinate-less plan node instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin,
  route leg with the arrival check, plan destination node, Google Maps
  link, and the show list constrained to what fits before it.
- Bookable places carry a partner pill on the plan (monetization):
  restaurants/cafés/pubs -> OpenTable, stations -> Trainline (Awin),
  hotels -> Booking.com, attractions -> GetYourGuide. Links work plainly
  today and start tagging referrals once the affiliate IDs in js/places.js
  are filled in (see its TO MONETIZE block); the footer discloses the
  commission.

The geocoder call was probed against the live API from an Actions runner
(the sandbox can't reach it): bounded=1 searches only amenity tags inside
the box — it misses Edinburgh Waverley entirely — so the search is
unbounded with a viewbox bias plus a client-side Edinburgh filter, and
same-named hits a block apart (station node vs building vs platforms)
dedupe with typed hits upgrading untyped ones. The captured responses are
committed as fixtures under js/__tests__/fixtures/nominatim/ and pin the
parser in js/__tests__/places.test.mjs (new js/ test glob wired into
package.json + scripts/verify.sh).

Closes #158

Rebasing onto main (the repo lands work squashed, so no merge commit)
surfaced two integration gaps between #155's remembered Now page and the
non-show destinations, previously caught while merging:

- planSnapshot/adoptRestoredPlan/restore-bar knew nothing of
  destPlace/destNote, so a saved place commitment restored as dead text —
  no pin, no plan. The snapshot now carries both (destPlace is plain
  JSON), pinned by a reload check in the browser-driven flow.
- Closing the constraint panel display:nones the time wheels, which
  clamps their scrollTop and fires a final scroll event; the settle
  handler read that as the user picking hours[0] and wiped the just-made
  commitment (reproduced via the restored-plan flow). It now ignores
  hidden wheels.

Full Chromium flow re-driven on the rebase: 16/16 checks. Refs #158

places: geocode 'Type a place' into real destinations, with partner booking links

The 'Not a show? Type a place' box previously stored a bare text label —
no pin, no route, no plan. Now 'Find on map' geocodes the query with
Nominatim (OpenStreetMap — no API key, matching the Leaflet/OSM stack):

- One match commits directly; several render candidate rows to pick from;
  none (or offline) falls back to keeping the text as a note, which now
  renders its own coordinate-less plan node instead of vanishing.
- A committed place behaves exactly like a committed show: violet map pin,
  route leg with the arrival check, plan destination node, Google Maps
  link, and the show list constrained to what fits before it.
- Bookable places carry a partner pill on the plan (monetization):
  restaurants/cafés/pubs -> OpenTable, stations -> Trainline (Awin),
  hotels -> Booking.com, attractions -> GetYourGuide. Links work plainly
  today and start tagging referrals once the affiliate IDs in js/places.js
  are filled in (see its TO MONETIZE block); the footer discloses the
  commission.

The geocoder call was probed against the live API from an Actions runner
(the sandbox can't reach it): bounded=1 searches only amenity tags inside
the box — it misses Edinburgh Waverley entirely — so the search is
unbounded with a viewbox bias plus a client-side Edinburgh filter, and
same-named hits a block apart (station node vs building vs platforms)
dedupe with typed hits upgrading untyped ones. The captured responses are
committed as fixtures under js/__tests__/fixtures/nominatim/ and pin the
parser in js/__tests__/places.test.mjs (new js/ test glob wired into
package.json + scripts/verify.sh).

Closes #158
